Internal Brief

The Blick LinkedIn programme is going live.

Three posts a week, every week. A steady drumbeat of real Blick work — site trials, product close-ups, technical know-how. Here's what's happening, why, and what to expect.

In one paragraph

We're starting a regular Blick LinkedIn programme: three posts a week, Monday / Wednesday / Friday. It kicks off with the Eco Dry trial video, and from there it's a steady drumbeat of real Blick work. You'll start seeing posts from the Blick page in your feed. There's nothing you need to do. This brief is just so you know what's happening, why, and what to expect.

What you'll see

Three post types on a weekly rhythm. Each has its own look so the page reads as a programme, not random content.

Monday
Site story
Real footage or photos from a job — customers, crews, results. The Eco Dry trial video is the first one.
Wednesday
Technical card
Dark editorial style. A drilling problem, explained simply, with a diagram. Plain English, no jargon.
Friday
Product hero
One product, big photo, minimal copy, one data point. Made to stop the scroll.

All three styles share the same Blick look (Blick Orange, Proxima Nova, real photos, accurate logo) so the page feels coherent as you scroll it.

Why we're doing it

  • WA growth. Australia is our biggest opportunity. LinkedIn is where decision-makers in that market actually look at suppliers. A consistent, credible page makes us easier to take seriously when Sales reaches out.
  • The competition is loud, not better. Most of our competitors post — but they post corporate stock-photo content. Real footage of real Blick work on real sites is genuinely different.
  • It compounds. One post is a flash. Three posts a week for a year is a body of work. We're playing the long game.

What's already done

  • Eco Dry trial post drafted, video edited (62 seconds), thumbnail picked, ready to go live.
  • Three-card visual template designed and published to the internal design library (now on v3 — Torque Down hero card for Fridays, dark technical card for Wednesdays).
  • Blick logo fixed and standardised across the whole template.
  • Brand voice, content rules, and visual identity locked in upstream so every post follows the same recipe.
  • CCL case study photos and signed release form in the bank for future posts.

How leads come in

When someone responds to a post (comment, DM, "interested" reaction), the call-to-action sends them to sales@blick.group. From there it's the normal sales flow. Nothing changes about how enquiries are handled. There's just likely to be more of them over time.

If you happen to be on a job

If something interesting happens — a tricky bore, a product working well, a clean site shot, a customer who's stoked with the result — flick a photo or short clip to Marketing. We'll keep building the bank.

Totally optional. Don't go out of your way.

Questions

Anything about the programme, the posts, or the assets — ask Shaun or Marketing.
